title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
content: We introduce the Transformer architecture which uses self-attention mechanisms to process sequences in parallel. The key innovation is the multi-head attention mechanism that allows the model to attend to different representation subspaces. This architecture forms the basis for modern LLMs.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce BERT, a new method for pre-training language representations. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
content: BERT introduces bidirectional pre-training using masked language modeling. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on various NLP tasks by fine-tuning on task-specific data. Key innovation: bidirectional context from both directions.

title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
abstract: We demonstrate that language models begin learning these tasks without explicit supervision when trained on a large corpus of text from the internet. GPT-2 is a large unsupervised language model.
content: GPT-2 demonstrates that a large language model trained on diverse internet text can perform various tasks in zero-shot and few-shot settings without task-specific training data.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
abstract: We find that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuned models.
content: GPT-3 scales up transformers to 175 billion parameters and demonstrates remarkable few-shot learning capabilities. The model can perform various tasks through in-context learning without explicit fine-tuning.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
abstract: While the Transformer architecture has become the de-facto standard for natural language processing tasks, its applications to computer vision remain limited. We show that a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform very well on image classification tasks.
content: Vision Transformer (ViT) applies transformer architecture to computer vision by treating images as sequences of patches. This demonstrates that transformers are universally applicable beyond NLP.

title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
abstract: As Transfer Learning from large-scale pre-trained models becomes more prevalent in Natural Language Processing (NLP), operating these large models in on-the-edge and/or under constrained computational training or inference budgets remains challenging.
content: DistilBERT uses knowledge distillation to create a smaller, faster version of BERT that retains 97% of its language understanding capabilities while being 40% smaller and 60% faster.

title: Efficient Transformers: A Survey
abstract: Transformers have become ubiquitous in machine learning, but they suffer from quadratic computational complexity. This survey comprehensively reviews efficient transformer variants that reduce computational requirements.
content: Comprehensive review of techniques to make transformers more efficient including sparse attention, approximations, and other optimizations. Covers linear transformers, local attention, and more.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are powerful models that have achieved excellent performance on difficult learning tasks. Although DNNs work well, they have a limitation: they can only process fixed-sized vectors as inputs and outputs.
content: Introduces the seq2seq model using LSTMs for machine translation. The encoder-decoder architecture became a foundation for many modern NLP systems including transformers.

title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
abstract: Transformers have achieved impressive results in the domain of language modeling. However, a critical shortcoming is the limited context length due to the quadratic memory requirements of self-attention.
content: Transformer-XL extends transformers to handle longer sequences through segment-level recurrence and relative positional encoding. Enables processing of documents with thousands of tokens.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
abstract: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters, but accessing this information only through a forward pass limits generalization to new or rare entities.
content: Introduces Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that combines a retrieval module with a generation module. Enables better performance on knowledge-intensive tasks like open-domain QA.
